mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date 2020-02-15; FEDFUNDS=1.55% at that time
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the rank information coefficient over triggered windows is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong export-led growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a genuine recession.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during supply-chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during periods of both rising rates and inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong mortgage credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k per month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 200000 for two consecutive months AND acceleration (second diff) > 0
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of wage stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% and 10% respectively in the same month signals a broad-based demand shock, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a synchronized economic downturn.
